target.title: feat(google): restore Antigravity auth provider boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This PR restores `google-antigravity` as a bundled Google auth provider while keeping the Google auth replacement boundary provider-owned, typed, and fail-closed.

The PR separates the three Google paths:

- `google-antigravity` is an Antigravity-owned session setup provider.
- `google-gemini-cli` imports the official Gemini CLI cache.
- `google` remains the Gemini API-key provider.

OpenClaw no longer needs to run a deprecated OpenClaw-owned Google browser callback flow for this replacement path.

This PR keeps Antigravity in scope, but it does not claim a live non-GUI Antigravity model backend. The current Antigravity implementation registers and gates the provider setup surface, documents the runtime boundary, and proves that OpenClaw does not silently wire an unproven runtime path.

The adjacent Gemini CLI path is hardened because it shares the Google auth replacement boundary. Official Gemini CLI cache import now requires validated active Google account identity before auth material is saved, refreshed, forwarded, or staged.

## What Changed

- Added bundled `google-antigravity` provider registration.
- Added Antigravity provider aliases and Google provider model/policy wiring.
- Added Antigravity setup text that points users to the signed-in Antigravity app session.
- Kept Antigravity setup provider-owned.
- Avoided starting an OpenClaw-owned Google browser callback flow.
- Avoided registering a `google-antigravity` CLI backend.
- Avoided writing default model config, runtime config, or auth material for Antigravity while no non-GUI runtime bridge is proven.
- Updated live-testing docs so Antigravity is not documented as a proven live gateway runtime until that bridge exists.
- Added official Gemini CLI cache import support for `google-gemini-cli`.
- Changed `google-gemini-cli` setup to import the official Gemini CLI cache instead of launching OpenClaw-owned Google browser auth.
- Required validated active Gemini CLI Google account identity during cache import.
- Failed closed when Gemini CLI account identity is missing or mismatched.
- Failed closed before save, refresh, forwarding, or runtime staging when account identity does not match.
- Preserved isolated Gemini CLI auth-home staging.
- Preserved inherited Google auth env clearing.
- Preserved Gemini API-key staging for `google` API-key profiles.
- Added provider-owned CLI backend auth resolution through `resolveCliBackendAuthCredential`.
- Preserved generic fallback forwarding only when no provider-owned hook exists.
- Made hook decline fail closed instead of falling through to generic forwarding.
- Preserved backend allowlist checks before and after auth resolution.
- Fixed CLI runner cleanup gaps on mid-prepare failures.
- Updated Google provider docs, live-testing docs, Plugin SDK exports/API baseline, and CLI backend plugin docs.

## Evidence

Validated locally through PR head `54eccc8b7e59b5aaaa2d14d675469a0b5445f4f2`.


Result: passed. 3 Vitest shards passed, 7 files passed, 248 tests passed.

Result: passed.

## Owner Acceptance

Provider owner acceptance: pending.

Plugin SDK owner acceptance: pending.

Security owner acceptance: pending.

## What Was Not Tested

I did not prove live non-GUI Antigravity model execution. The targeted live gateway sweep selected `google-antigravity/gemini-3-flash` and found no runnable `google-antigravity` auth setup. That confirms the current safe boundary: this PR registers and gates Antigravity setup, but does not claim runtime model execution until a real Antigravity runtime bridge exists.

I did not perform a live Gemini CLI Google account login. The Gemini CLI path is covered by deterministic cache-import, account identity validation, refresh, forwarding, and staging tests.

I did not run the full repository test suite. The focused suites cover the changed Google provider registration, Antigravity setup behavior, Gemini CLI account identity validation, CLI auth forwarding boundary, docs, types, SDK surface, and proof behavior.

## Tests

AI-assisted: yes.

## Real behavior proof

Latest proof file: `/home/rev/pr-98343-antigravity-live-proof.txt`

Antigravity provider proof for commit `54eccc8b7e59b5aaaa2d14d675469a0b5445f4f2`:

- Verified pushed PR head matches local HEAD: `54eccc8b7e59b5aaaa2d14d675469a0b5445f4f2`.
- Verified installed Antigravity binary: `/usr/bin/antigravity`.
- Verified installed Antigravity version: `1.107.0`.
- Verified `antigravity --help` command surface.
- Verified `antigravity chat --help` command surface.
- Verified OpenClaw registers `google-antigravity` as a bundled provider.
- Verified OpenClaw wires `google-antigravity` through Google provider policy/model registration paths.
- Verified OpenClaw does not register a `google-antigravity` CLI backend.
- Verified the provider does not write a default model, config patch, or agent runtime config while no non-GUI Antigravity runtime API is proven.
- Verified focused Google provider tests pass.
- Verified SDK checks pass: `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` and `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`.
- Verified test-type and docs checks pass.
- Verified diff hygiene with `git diff --check`.
- Verified combined proof file passed leak check.
- Verified targeted live gateway sweep reaches `google-antigravity` candidate selection and confirms no runnable runtime bridge is currently claimed.

Targeted live gateway boundary command:

```text
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$HOME/pr-98343-antigravity-live-proof/openclaw.live-antigravity.json" OPENCLAW_LIVE_GATEWAY_PROVIDERS="google-antigravity" OPENCLAW_LIVE_GATEWAY_MODELS="google-antigravity/gemini-3-flash" pnpm test:live src/gateway/gateway-models.profiles.live.test.ts
```

Result: boundary confirmed. The live harness selected `google-antigravity/gemini-3-flash`, reached auth candidate resolution, and found no runnable `google-antigravity` setup. This PR therefore does not claim live non-GUI Antigravity model execution.
